steps.name: 01-help-lstart
stdout: usage: kathara lstart [-h] [--noterminals | --terminals] [--privileged] [-d DIRECTORY] [-F] [-l] [-o [METADATA ...]] [--terminal-emu TERMINAL_EMU] [--print] [--no-hosthome | --hosthome]
[--no-shared | --shared] [--exclude DEVICE_NAME [DEVICE_NAME ...]]
[DEVICE_NAME ...]
Start a Kathara network scenario
positional arguments:
DEVICE_NAME           Launches only specified devices.
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
--noterminals         Start the network scenario without opening terminal windows.
--terminals           Start the network scenario opening terminal windows.
--privileged          Start the devices in privileged mode. MUST BE ROOT FOR THIS OPTION.
-d, --directory DIRECTORY
Specify the folder containing the network scenario.
-F, --force-lab       Force the network scenario to start without a lab.conf or lab.dep file.
-l, --list            Show information about running devices after the network scenario has been started.
-o, --pass [METADATA ...]
Apply metadata to all devices of a network scenario during startup.
--terminal-emu TERMINAL_EMU
Set a different terminal emulator application (Unix only).
--print, --dry-mode   Open the lab.conf file and check if it is correct (dry run).
--no-hosthome, -H     Do not mount "/hosthome" directory inside devices.
--hosthome            Mount "/hosthome" directory inside devices.
--no-shared, -S       Do not mount "/shared" directory inside devices.
--shared              Mount "/shared" directory inside devices.
--exclude DEVICE_NAME [DEVICE_NAME ...]
Exclude specified devices from startup.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 04-help-linfo
stdout: usage: kathara linfo [-h] [-d DIRECTORY] [-w | -c] [-n DEVICE_NAME | -t]
Show information about a Kathara network scenario
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
-d, --directory DIRECTORY
Specify the folder containing the network scenario.
-w, -l, --watch, --live
Watch mode, can be used only when a network scenario is launched.
-c, --conf            Read static information from lab.conf.
-n, --name DEVICE_NAME
Show only information about a specified device.
-t, --topology        Get running topology info
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 05-help-lconfig
stdout: usage: kathara lconfig [-h] [-d LAB_PATH] -n DEVICE_NAME (--add CD/MAC [CD/MAC ...] | --rm CD [CD ...])
Manage the network interfaces of a running Kathara device in a Kathara network scenario
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
-d, --directory LAB_PATH
Path of the network scenario to configure, if not specified the current path is used
-n, --name DEVICE_NAME
Name of the device to configure.
--add CD/MAC [CD/MAC ...]
Specify the collision domain to add.
--rm CD [CD ...]      Specify the collision domain to remove.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 06-help-list
stdout: usage: kathara list [-h] [-a] [-w] [-n DEVICE_NAME]
Show all running Kathara devices of the current user
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
-a, --all             Show all running Kathara devices of all users. MUST BE ROOT FOR THIS OPTION.
-w, -l, --watch, --live
Watch mode.
-n, --name DEVICE_NAME
Show only information about a specified device.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 07-help-wipe
stdout: usage: kathara wipe [-h] [-f] [-s | -a]
Delete all Kathara devices and collision domains, optionally also delete settings
options:
-h, --help      Show a help message and exit.
-f, --force     Force the wipe.
-s, --settings  Wipe the stored settings of the current user.
-a, --all       Wipe all Kathara devices and collision domains of all users. MUST BE ROOT FOR THIS OPTION.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 08-help-check
stdout: usage: kathara check [-h]
Check your system environment
options:
-h, --help  Show a help message and exit.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 09-help-connect
stdout: usage: kathara connect [-h] [-d DIRECTORY | -v] [--shell SHELL] [-l] DEVICE_NAME
Connect to a Kathara device
positional arguments:
DEVICE_NAME           Name of the device to connect to.
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
-d, --directory DIRECTORY
Specify the folder containing the network scenario.
-v, --vmachine        The device has been started with vstart command.
--shell SHELL         Shell that should be used inside the device.
-l, --logs            Print device startup logs before launching the shell.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki

steps.name: 10-help-exec
stdout: usage: kathara exec [-h] [-d DIRECTORY | -v] [--no-stdout] [--no-stderr] [--wait] DEVICE_NAME COMMAND [COMMAND ...]
Execute a command in a Kathara device
positional arguments:
DEVICE_NAME           Name of the device to execute the command into.
COMMAND               Shell command that will be executed inside the device.
options:
-h, --help            Show a help message and exit.
-d, --directory DIRECTORY
Specify the folder containing the network scenario.
-v, --vmachine        The device has been started with vstart command.
--no-stdout           Disable stdout of the executed command.
--no-stderr           Disable stderr of the executed command.
--wait                Wait until startup commands execution finishes.
For examples and further information visit: https://github.com/KatharaFramework/Kathara/wiki
